aspects.name: Relationships and couple time
aspects.digest: On 2024-05-02, Crystal Wilson asked how to adjust her schedule for more quality time with James. By 2024-11-20, she was worried about their evening time during pilot launch week. She planned weekly Friday dinners with James and approved a monthly date night; the first Saturday at 7:00 PM was only an example, not confirmed.

aspects.name: Personal background
aspects.digest: Crystal Wilson lives in East Janethaven, Montserrat, which she describes as beautiful but distracting. Crystal Wilson earns about $85,000 annually.

aspects.name: Time management and scheduling
aspects.digest: 03/14/2024: Crystal declined a 3 PM meeting to protect her 9 AM writing block, then said she felt stressed; on 03/15 she said she had never done this before. She prefers morning creative focus and wants to balance meetings without guilt. She aimed to cut work from 50 to 40 hours weekly by July 2024; by 09/05 she was at 42. She later rescheduled a 09/01 client call from 3 to 11 AM, gaining two hours. On 11/20 she chose an 8 AM start. She uses Google Calendar synced with a Moleskine planner and blocks weekday 9 AM two-hour creative sessions.

A later June 30 deadline and milestone schedule were assistant suggestions, not confirmed. On 05-02 she considered shifting focus to casting while continuing writing. aspects.name: Pilot production planning and deadlines
aspects.digest: Mar. 1, 2024: Crystal endorsed a plan for pre-production Mar.–Apr., filming May, and post-production by June 30, with a $120,000 cap; she prioritized script finalization. By May 2, casting delays had pushed delivery to July 15 (stakeholders told Apr. 28). On July 5, 12/16 scenes were filmed and post-production was 60% underway. Nov. 20: final sound mix due Nov. 22, final cut Dec. 5, release Dec. 15.

aspects.name: Pilot budget and expense tracking
aspects.digest: From 2024-03-15 to 2024-06-30, Crystal Wilson endorsed a proposed $120,000 pilot budget: $30,000 pre-production, $60,000 production, and $30,000 post-production. On 2024-05-02, she asked to track expenses against a $5,000 post-production software-license allocation; actual spending was unspecified. Guidance included recording and reviewing transactions; an example of $2,500 spent and $2,500 remaining was not confirmed. Since 2024-11-20, financial decisions require explicitly confirming budget amounts.

aspects.name: Pilot casting and location scouting
aspects.digest: On 2024-03-28, after casting director Heather recommended early auditions, Crystal shifted from scriptwriting to casting; by 2024-04-20, she celebrated finishing casting with a $120 dinner for four at The Coral Reef. In early May, after the script was finalized, she agreed to start location scouting. On 2024-05-02, she said she’d never scouted with Jeremy and asked about collaborating despite schedule conflicts, including reviewing recorded videos if he couldn’t livestream.

aspects.name: Task, reminder, and project-management systems
aspects.digest: On 2024-03-15, Crystal Wilson planned to use Google Calendar synced with iPhone for production-call alerts 24 hours ahead and separate iPhone Reminders lists; she might explore IFTTT/Zapier later. On 2024-05-02, she praised Trello for pilot-task tracking and said Todoist, synced with Google Calendar, raised task completion by 25%; weekend reminders were only under consideration. On 2024-09-05, she hired Michele for 20 hours/week at $25/hour; calendar and task support were suggested, not confirmed.

aspects.name: Task batching and productivity
aspects.digest: On Mar. 15, 2024, Crystal Wilson planned a four-week trial of Friday email batching (2–5 p.m.) to save 3 hours weekly. By July 10, she reported batching emails and calls on Mondays and Fridays since June 1, saving 4 hours weekly, though stressed. In September, records both say she was applying Deep Work techniques and had never read the book and was considering it. She prioritizes batching similar tasks.

aspects.name: Meeting and calendar coordination
aspects.digest: On March 15, 2024, Crystal Wilson planned to ask to reschedule a March 14 meeting; suggested alternative times were drafts, not confirmed availability or a sent message. On March 29, she said she moved a client meeting from 11 a.m. to 4 p.m., gaining three morning writing hours; by May 2, she was unsure it was right. On July 10, she used recurring Google Calendar reminders for family events, synced with partner James’s calendar, and sought optimization advice; suggested improvements were not confirmed as adopted.

A no-work-Sundays rule began June 30 and helped, though on Nov 20 she also said she instituted it since Nov 3 and worried about productivity. In July she chose Adobe over Final Cut Pro, citing $150 in retraining savings, and finalized four sound-mixing sessions with Jeremy for $600. aspects.name: Workload, scheduling, and boundaries
aspects.digest: 2024-06-20: Crystal Wilson hired Stephanie’s agency for social media management at $800/month after Laura advised delegation. By 2024-07-10, workload impact was unreported; the assistant suggested clear goals, check-ins, and tracking growth, engagement, and website traffic. Starting 2024-07-01, Crystal added daily one-hour buffer slots, reporting 35% less deadline stress.

aspects.name: schedule buffer advice
aspects.digest: The assistant endorsed Crystal Wilson's daily one-hour buffer slots as a good scheduling decision, citing flexibility and reduced stress, and suggested reviewing whether the slots are used effectively. This was advice, not a separately confirmed user preference.

aspects.name: Family and school activities
aspects.digest: On July 10, 2024, Crystal Wilson said Rachel Wilson’s school requested more parental involvement. Crystal negotiated to attend monthly meetings, saving 3 hours per month. The assistant called this reasonable and suggested other ways to support Rachel, but Crystal did not say she adopted them.

aspects.name: Financial planning and event expenses
aspects.digest: On July 10, 2024, Crystal Wilson said Sunday meal prep cut weekday cooking by 1 hour and takeout spending by $50 per week. She asked how to save more time and money; batch cooking, meal planning, bulk staples, leftovers, and other ideas were suggested but not confirmed as actions.

aspects.name: upcoming projects
aspects.digest: Crystal Wilson co-hosted a 90-minute virtual brainstorming session with Stephanie on September 3, 2024, for their upcoming projects.

aspects.name: Pilot milestones and celebrations
aspects.digest: On September 3, 2024, Crystal Wilson celebrated reaching 90% completion of her pilot with a six-person team at The Coral Reef for $180. By December 20, she was planning a family celebration there for eight guests, budgeting $300 and unsure if it would cover food and drinks.

aspects.name: Pilot marketing and launch
aspects.digest: On Nov 1, 2024, Crystal Wilson began reserving two-hour Monday and Wednesday slots to prepare marketing for the pilot planned for Dec 15. On Nov 10, Laura recommended audience-engagement strategies, which Crystal felt would help. On Nov 20, Crystal approved $3,500 for Facebook and Instagram ads and rejected a proposed $5,000 influencer campaign; no rationale or results were recorded. She sought deadline advice while keeping her no-calls-after-6-PM launch-week agreement.
